_doc: Loop-closure retirement ledger (plan:kura-tagger-self-improvement-loop, user 2026-07-22 'veto の base 昇格・退役'). A gated-veto head is RETIRED once the base model absorbs its correction — either a logit-patch reaches the metric floor without the veto, or a base fine-tune (tagger/train_base_finetune.py) improves the backbone so the base+patch no longer over-produces the gate tag. build_release.py skips bundling any gate listed in `retired`, so the release stops carrying a redundant post-pass probe; the tag stays in the reap domain via its patched row (reap_domain = patched ∪ veto), so cancellation continues through the base. This is how the loop closes instead of vetoes accumulating forever.

log.why: v2 logit patch (stock row @0.31, tagger_patch id=93) clears the metric floor WITHOUT the veto (P 0.8952 / R 0.7899, bootstrap 0.8755, 0 single-flip breaks, on the 293-row GT). The veto (sha b1c47604) was calibrated against v1 firing set and does not generalize: on the 198 GT rows it never saw, v1+veto reads P 0.3556 / R 0.50 while v2 alone reads P 0.6667 / R 0.6875. Keeping it on top of v2 would only cut recall. Retired per the loop-closure rule: the base+patch absorbed the correction; the tag stays in the reap domain via its patched row.
